study: Descriptive CLI evaluation on one authored four-entry arithmetic table

definitions.quality: Four correct and four defective starts per setting. Missing terminal outcomes retain their scheduled denominator and [0,1] bounds.
definitions.first_step: Among initially defective starts, a valid first repair with a correct result; observed before any later requested check. Later loss cannot erase an observed first action.
definitions.resources: All recorded invocations include technical failures. Complete-episode comparisons use only completed episodes. An unchanged repair resubmits exactly the same table.
definitions.shortest_success: Among terminally correct episodes only, the feasible minimum is 1 decision (stop) for a correct start and 2 (repair then stop) for a defective start. An action above that minimum may be informative.
definitions.time: Episode active time sums CLI subprocess durations in that episode. Overall capture span is first recorded start to last recorded finish, including gaps and concurrent workers.
definitions.tokens: Input and output form the total. Cached input and reasoning output are separately reported subcounts when present. Missing usage stays unknown. Token counts do not establish cost.
definitions.paired_effect: High minus low on the identical case_id in the same model. All signs are numerical. For decisions, latency and tokens, a negative difference denotes less use at high. Ties are retained.
definitions.scope: Effort and model are requested CLI settings. Observed runtime metadata cannot attest model weights or internal reasoning. Repeated starts from one task give no general model ranking.
